![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/31d4236bf58cd579c49c7259c32a2a9171e07c771b4c34040ac92896809f695f.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $x=\frac{2}{y}$ and $x=3-y$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=-2.$ Which of the following gives the volume of the resulting solid?
question.worked_solution:
First, we want to determine the limits of integration. We find the intersections of the curves by solving the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{y} & =3-y \\ 2 & =3y-{y}^{2} \\ {y}^{2}-3y+2 & =0 \\ (y-1)(y-2) & =0 \\ y & =1,2\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, our limits of integration are from $y=1$ to $y=2.$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/b73c341f4d09b1df7bea162bc7dbe10d0ee60920c847f9c24210386a3d139e61.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=\frac{2}{y},$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x=3-y.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x=3-y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/c8c8e766c66e47a54f316f54893d603b245acec8f529da3a5033d2bba547a319.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(3-y)-(-2)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[5-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=\frac{2}{y}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14215763/assets/1b31331f1c0da353bee6fe29d10e9e58dd531cbc8152cbce214d1adea771b032.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[\,(\frac{2}{y})-(-2)\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{2}{y}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[5-y]}^{2}\,\text{d}y-\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}{[\frac{2}{y}+2]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{1}^{2}({[5-y]}^{2}-{[\frac{2}{y}+2]}^{2})\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
